pages.text: We depend on plastic. Now we’re drowning in it. | National Geographic By Laura Parker Photographs by Randy Olson Last updated April 8, 2026 This story originally published in the June 2018 issue of National Geographic magazine. See more digitized stories from our archives here . If plastic had been invented when the Pilgrims sailed from Plymouth, England, to North America—and the Mayflower had been stocked with bottled water and plastic-wrapped snacks—their plastic trash would likely still be around, four centuries later. If the Pilgrims had been like many people today and simply tossed their empty bottles and wrappers over the side, Atlantic waves and sunlight would have worn all that plastic into tiny bits. And those bits might still be floating around the world’s oceans today, sponging up toxins to add to the ones already in them, waiting to be eaten by some hapless fish or oyster, and ultimately perhaps by one of us. We should give thanks that the Pilgrims didn’t have plastic, I thought recently as I rode a train to Plymouth along England’s south coast. I was on my way to see a man who would help me make sense of the whole mess we’ve made with plastic, especially in the ocean. After sheets of clear plastic trash have been washed in the Buriganga River, in Dhaka, Bangladesh, Noorjahan spreads them out to dry, turning them regularly— while also tending to her son, Momo. The plastic will eventually be sold to a recycler. Less than a fifth of all plastic gets recycled globally. In the U.S. it’s less than 10 percent. We need union recognition to safeguard our jobs Wed 18 Nov 2026 06.50 EST Last modified on Wed 18 Nov 2026 07.27 EST Share W hen I first got the call offering me a job at Rockstar, I was thrilled. I thought back to being a child and sneaking into my brother’s room to grab the PlayStation Portable so I could secretly play Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories. The same kid who fell in love with Rockstar’s games back then now gets to spend every day helping to create those worlds as an animation programmer at the studio in Edinburgh. This week, we will celebrate the culmination of more than a decade of effort: the release of the most anticipated game of all time, Grand Theft Auto VI . But our team has the opportunity to make history a second time this month. Right now, the ballot is open for Rockstar employees to decide whether we want the union we have built with our colleagues to get recognition. As someone who cares deeply about our team, cares about what we do, and wants us to be able to keep delivering world-class games into the future, I’m voting yes.

It’s called Earth Overshoot Day . In 1971, it fell on Dec. 25. Disturbingly, by 2022, it fell on July 28. In short, we humans need 1.75 Earths to support our current rate of consumption! pages.text: We Sent a Cartographer to the Sale of One of America's Most Famous Maps | National Geographic By Nina Strochlic Published October 29, 2026 1:09 On a spring day in 1982, a never-before-sold piece went under the hammer at Christie's auction house in New York City. In a moment he later said left him breathless, Malcolm Forbes, Jr., the president of Forbes magazine, raised his paddle and won the hand-drawn survey of the Mason-Dixon Line for $360,000—the most ever spent on an American map at the time. The sale shocked bidders: As the price climbed to more than 20 times its estimated sale price, it also managed to overshadow a rare copy of the Declaration of Independence (which fetched $285,000). The losing bidder for the Mason-Dixon map was the Library of Congress. Forbes ended up with an unusual-looking relic: six sheets of paper conjoined into a manuscript just six and a half inches tall and over six feet long. It’s believed to be the only original copy of the western section of the Mason Dixon survey—the most famous border in America. ( Why Your Mental Map of the World Is (Probably) Wrong .) More than 40 years later, that same map has now sold for $1,187,500 to an anonymous buyer, according to Brunk Auctions in North Carolina. The bidding started at $400,000, a sale price that doubled within mere minutes. Today, the Mason-Dixon Line is synonymous with a divided America, and its darkest era. WoT provides standardized building blocks that simplify IoT application development by applying the well-established Web paradigm. This approach boosts flexibility and interoperability, especially for cross-domain scenarios, while enabling reuse of proven standards and tooling. WoT unlocks the commercial potential held back by IoT fragmentation. Use Cases The Web of Things technologies apply to a variety of domains and unlock use cases. pages.text: Web of Things Working Group Charter Web of Things Working Group Charter The mission of the Web of Things Working Group is to maintain and extend the family of WoT deliverables with new functionalities to support desired use cases. This work supports the overarching mission of the Web of Things to counteract fragmentation in the Internet of Things (IoT) by providing building blocks that enable seamless integration of devices and services across the IoT ecosystem. Join the Web of Things Working Group. Charter Status See the group status page and detailed change history . Face-to-face: we will meet during the W3C's annual Technical Plenary week; additional face-to-face meetings may be scheduled by consent of the participants, usually no more than 3 per year. Motivation and Background In recent years, the Web of Things (WoT) Working Group has developed a set of deliverables that address interoperability challenges in the IoT. These deliverables define standardized building blocks, such as the WoT Thing Description , WoT Discovery , and WoT Scripting API , which simplify IoT device onboarding into target systems and applications, as well as IoT application development, by using well-established Web technologies. pages.description: The Web of Things (WoT) Working Group rechartered for two years to improve IoT interoperability and address physical AI use cases. WoT counteracts fragmentation in IoT by providing building blocks that enable seamless device integration across smart buildings, industrial automation, and energy management. Drawing on Plugfest insights, the new charter focuses on enhancing Thing Description expressiveness, introducing protocol bindings, and guiding AI agents.
pages.text: Web of Things Working Group recharter: New momentum for IoT interoperability | 2026 | Blog | W3C Skip to content Web of Things Working Group recharter: New momentum for IoT interoperability Part of Developers Author(s) and publish date By: Ege Korkan, specification editor, on behalf of the WoT Working Group Published: 21 October 2026 On 14 September 2026, the Web of Things (WoT) Working Group rechartered, announcing the agenda for the next two years. The group plans to further improve interoperability across the Internet of Things (IoT) and address emerging use cases around physical AI. WoT counteracts fragmentation in IoT by providing building blocks that enable seamless integration of devices and services across the IoT ecosystem. Across domains like smart buildings, industrial automation, and energy management, it eliminates proprietary silos and significantly reduces integration effort. With metadata added at the device level, semantic data quality improves across all layers, reducing the need for manual intervention downstream. Web of Things across multiple ecosystems WoT adopts architectural ideas and technologies from the web, which built an interoperability layer for the Internet, and applies them to IoT. Rather than proposing a new standard or protocol to replace existing ones, it creates an abstraction layer that allows different protocols and standards to work together. pages.description: 「Web of Things（WoT）」ワーキンググループは、IoTの相互運用性を向上させ、物理的なAIのユースケースに対応するため、2年間の活動指針を更新しました。WoTは、スマートビル、産業オートメーション、エネルギー管理の分野にわたって、デバイスをシームレスに統合するための構成要素を提供することで、IoTにおける断片化の解消に取り組んでいます。Plugfestで得られた知見を踏まえ、新たな活動指針では、「Thing Description」の表現力の向上、プロトコルバインディングの導入、およびAIエージェントの指針策定に重点を置いています。

pages.text: Web Standards | W3C Skip to content Web Standards Web standards are blueprints –or building blocks– of a consistent and harmonious digitally connected world. They are implemented in browsers, blogs, search engines, and other software that power our experience on the web. The promise of web standards W3C standards define an open web platform for application development. The web has the unprecedented potential to enable developers to build rich interactive experiences, that can be available on any device. The platform continues to expand, but web users have long ago rallied around HTML as the cornerstone of the web. Many more technologies that W3C and its partners are creating extend the web and give it full strength, including CSS, SVG, WOFF, WebRTC, XML, and a growing variety of APIs. Read more about W3C Standards Why W3C web standards? W3C publishes recommendations, that are considered web standards. W3C develops technical specifications according to the W3C Process , which is designed to maximize consensus, ensure quality, earn endorsement and adoption by W3C Members and the broader community. W3C web standards are optimized for interoperability, security, privacy, web accessibility, and internationalization. W3C's proven web standards process is based on fairness, openness, royalty-free, we make the web work — for everyone. Learn about the potential and promises of web standards. pages.text: Web标准 | W3C 转到内容 Web标准 Web标准作为蓝图或构建模块被用来构建一致且和谐的数字互联世界，这些标准应用到了浏览器、博客、搜索引擎及其他支持Web体验的软件中。 Web标准的承诺 W3C标准定义了一个 开放的Web平台 用于应用开发。Web拥有前所未有的潜能，使开发者能够构建丰富的、可以在任何设备上使用的互动体验。 Web平台不断扩展，实际上Web用户早已围绕HTML这个Web基石汇聚起来。W3C及其合作伙伴创建的更多技术扩展了Web并增强了其功能，包括CSS、SVG、WOFF、WebRTC、XML及越来越多的各种API。 了解W3C标准 为什么选择W3C发布的Web标准？ W3C发布的推荐标准被视为Web标准。 W3C根据 W3C标准化流程文档 制定技术规范，该流程旨在最大限度地达成共识、确保质量，并获得 W3C会员 及更广泛社区的认可和采纳。 W3C制定的Web标准在互操作性、安全性、隐私保护、Web无障碍和国际化层面进行了优化。 W3C经过验证的Web标准化流程基于公平、开放和免版税的原则，我们致力于打造一个所有人都可以使用的Web。 了解Web标准的潜力和承诺。 在W3C创建标准的价值 自1994年以来，W3C一直为创建Web标准提供一个高效的环境： 遵循基于共识的决策流程； 满足无障碍、隐私、安全性和国际化的要求； 反映各个行业和全球利益相关者的意见； 平衡速度、公平、公众责任和质量； 受益于参与者提供的 免版税专利许可承诺 ； 保持稳定持久（W3C确保标准发布的URI持续有效）； 受益于W3C内外各团体的广泛审查； 免费提供； 通过互用性测试得到强化。 广泛的应用范围 W3C的 标准、技术规范和指南 在Web上被广泛应用： 渲染网页； 任意设备均可以访问； Web的架构； 链接的数据和服务； 创作工具。 相关内容 W3C标准和草案 本页面列出了处于各个成熟度级别的W3C所有工作组的全部标准和规范。 目录 W3C的小组 该页面列出了W3C的各类工作小组。 目录 审阅与公众反馈 对规范、实现、测试套件和代码的公众评审与反馈。 页面

pages.text: Web標準 | W3C コンテンツへスキップ Web標準 Web標準は、一貫性があり調和のとれたデジタル接続された世界の青写真、あるいは構成要素です。ブラウザ、ブログ、検索エンジン、その他のソフトウェアに実装され、私たちのウェブ体験を支えています。 Web標準の約束 W3C 標準は、アプリケーション開発のための オープンなウェブプラットフォーム を定義しています。Webは、開発者がどのようなデバイスでも利用できるリッチなインタラクティブな経験を構築できる、前例のない可能性を秘めています。 プラットフォームは拡大し続けているが、ウェブ・ユーザーはとっくにHTMLをウェブの礎として結集しています。W3Cとそのパートナーは、CSS、SVG、WOFF、WebRTC、XML、そして増え続けるさまざまなAPIなど、ウェブを拡張し、ウェブの完全な強度を与える多くの技術を生み出しています。 W3C標準について詳しく読む なぜW3Cのウェブ標準なのか？ W3Cはウェブ標準とみなされる勧告を発表しています。 W3C は、 W3C プロセス に従って技術仕様を開発しています。このプロセスは、コンセンサスを最大化し、品質を保証し、 W3C 会員 やより広範なコミュニティによる支持と採用を得るように設計されています。 W3CのWeb標準は、相互運用性、セキュリティ、プライバシー、Webアクセシビリティ、国際化のために最適化されています。 W3C の実績あるWeb標準プロセスは、公平性、オープン性、ロイヤリティフリーに基づいており、すべての人のために Web を機能させています。 Web標準の持つ可能性と約束されたものについて学びましょう｡ W3Cで標準を作る価値 1994年以来、W3Cはウェブ標準を作成するための生産的な環境を提供してきました： 合意に基づく意思決定プロセスに従う アクセシビリティ、プライバシー、セキュリティ、国際化に対応する 多様な業界や世界中の利害関係者の意見を反映する 速度、公平性、公共の責任、品質のバランスをとる 参加者からの ロイヤリティフリーの特許ライセンスのコミットメント の恩恵を受ける 安定しており（W3Cは発行されたURIでの持続性を保証する） W3C内外のグループから広範なレビューを受ける 無料で利用可能 相互運用性テストを通じて強化される 幅広い用途 W3C 標準、技術仕様、およびガイドライン は、ウェブ上で広く展開されています： Web ページのレンダリング あらゆるデバイスからのアクセスが可能 Webのアーキテクチャ データとサービスのリンク オーサリングツール 参考 W3C の標準と草稿 このページでは、あらゆる成熟度レベルの、あらゆるW3C作業部会による、すべてのW3C標準と仕様をリストアップしています。 ディレクトリー一覧 W3CのWeb標準について このページでは、ワールド・ワイド・ウェブ・コンソーシアムでオープンなウェブ標準を作成することの価値など、W3Cのウェブ標準について詳しく説明します。 ページ レビューと公開フィードバック 仕様、実装、テスト・スイート、コードに関する公開レビューとフィードバック。 ページ 私たちの使命 W3Cとは何か、W3Cの価値観、そして、ウェブの可能性を最大限に引き出すというW3Cの使命に基づく原則についてご紹介します。 ページ

pages.text: Weirdest Minor League jerseys Skip to Content Benjamin Hill travels the nation collecting stories about what makes Minor League Baseball unique. This excerpt from the Baseball Traveler newsletter, presented by Circle K, is a mere taste of the smorgasbord of delights he offers every week. Read the full newsletter here , and subscribe to his newsletter here . They took the field in those jerseys?! No corner of the sports world has prompted this incredulous query more than Minor League Baseball, whose teams regularly wear outlandish theme jerseys in addition to their regular uniforms. To be a Minor League fan is to be exposed, on a daily basis, to a cornucopia of bold colors and bolder design. Check out jerseys in the MiLB Shop Ten examples of some of the boldest –- and probably the weirdest -- can be found below, all of which debuted during the era of sartorial excess that was the 2010s. Let's take a trip down memory lane, marveling anew at these groundbreaking and bizarre Minor League jerseys. (Note: Teams are listed at their current affiliation and level of play, which may have changed since the time these jerseys were first worn.) Bacon-themed uniforms (Lehigh Valley IronPigs, Triple-A PHI, 2014) Like Dylan going electric in 1965, the IronPigs' bacon-themed duds were an epochal event that firmly delineated the start of a new era. These uniforms, featuring bacon-strip hats and jerseys with a strip of bacon underneath a "'Pigs" wordmark, planted the seed for the food-themed alternate identity craze that continues in the Minor Leagues to this day. pages.text: Welcome Baseball Fans! | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Welcome Baseball Fans! If you're a fan of baseball and disability employment, you've come to the right place! At the U.S. Department of Labor's Office of Disability Employment Policy (ODEP), we work to increase success for people with disabilities in America's workplaces. This is a goal we share with our Alliance partner the Professional Baseball Athletic Trainers Society (PBATS). Over the years, ODEP and PBATS have collaborated on a number of activities, including the production of several public service announcements (PSAs) featuring former MLB players with disabilities and/or professional baseball athletic trainers from clubs around the country. Among the topics these PSAs address is the importance of helping people stay at or return to work after injury or illness and, most recently, strategies for fostering mental health-friendly workplaces. Please view and share these PSAs and explore our resources for fostering supportive workplaces, for all workers in all types of workplaces—because everyone should be in the game.
